findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination cannot build cursors from datetimes
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint configures this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this method applies `math.floor` or `math.ceil` directly to the datetime value. Those functions require a real number, so an optimized request with results raises `TypeError` while building the cursor instead of returning a page. The datetime-specific conversion used by `DateTimePaginator` is needed here as well.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to a queryset slice
findings.body: When advanced pagination receives a cursor with a negative offset, this branch passes that offset directly to a Django queryset slice. Django does not support negative queryset indices and raises `ValueError`; it does not clamp or otherwise handle them as the comment claims. Such a cursor therefore causes the request to fail rather than paginate.
